newsitem.title: USA: Austrian economy minister urges open Asian markets.
newsitem.headline: Austrian economy minister urges open Asian markets.

text.p: Europe and the United States should work together to pry open markets in Asia, Austrian Economic Affairs Minister Hannes Farnleitner said Friday.
Farnleitner, visiting the United States, said that markets in Asia are still surrounded by trade and investment barriers and that a joint effort was needed to help get them open.
"We should join forces to get freer access to Asian markets," Farnleitner told a briefing for reporters.
He is due to meet with deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang and Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat.
He said it was important that Russia and China join the World Trade Organization since they have become large trading nations -- a pattern that will likely grow in the future.
He criticized U.S. policy of keeping an embargo on Cuba and said this and issues surrounding the Helms-Burton legislation will likely come up during his discussions here.
"An embargo is the safest way to keep Mr. Castro in power," Farnleitner told reporters.
He also was critical of embargoes against Libya and Iran, saying the Europeans and Congress should hold a dialogue so that regulations are not suddenly put on Europe's front door.
"Let's take the heat out of this discussion," he said.
